note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. Warner's primary was canceled (unopposed); GOP primary held Aug 4.

VA-senate.statusNote: Sen. Mark Warner (D), seeking a fourth term, faces retired Army Maj. Gen. Bert Mizusawa (R), who won the Aug 4 primary with about 51%.

candidates.name: Mark Warner
candidates.now: U.S. Senator; Vice Chair, Senate Intelligence Committee
candidates.background: Virginia's senior senator since 2009 and former governor (2002-2006), who left office with 71% approval. Made a telecom venture-capital fortune before politics. Seeking a fourth term.

cost.label: Focused on 'lowering costs for families, growing wages'; cites $2,900+ in added family costs from tariffs (Senate priorities)

health.label: Early ACA champion who wants to move 'towards a universal coverage model'; defend Medicaid, protect rural hospitals (Senate priorities)

housing.label: Backs bipartisan bills for new construction and first-time-buyer down-payment help; ROAD to Housing Act (Senate priorities)

immigration.label: 'A meaningful pathway to citizenship with secure borders'; DREAM Act; opposes 'inhumane mass round-ups' (Senate priorities)

taxes.label: Wants the wealthiest and corporations 'paying their fair share'; close 'unfair tax loopholes' (Senate priorities)

climate.label: 'All-of-the-above' energy independence: defends offshore wind and nuclear; 'practical, science-based' emissions reduction (Senate priorities)

education.label: College affordability and student-debt relief; industry certifications and non-4-year pathways (Senate priorities)

safety.label: Mixed: prevention plus accountability; body cameras, modern forensics, bipartisan anti-fentanyl work (Senate priorities)

repro.label: Co-introduced the Women's Health Protection Act: decisions 'between a woman and her doctor, not politicians' (Senate release)

democracy.label: Co-sponsor of the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act: 'ensure that every American can make their voice heard' (Senate release)

candidates.name: Bert Mizusawa
candidates.now: Retired Army Major General; consulting-firm CEO
candidates.background: Retired two-star Army general, first in his 1979 West Point class, awarded the Silver Star for a 1984 action at the Korean DMZ. Harvard-trained attorney and former deputy undersecretary of the Army; foreign policy adviser to the 2016 Trump campaign. Won the Aug 4 Republican primary with about 51%.
priorities: Simplify the tax code; attack fraudulent spending

cost.label: Reduce costs for 'farmers, small businesses and working families' through deregulation and American energy (Charlottesville Tomorrow)

immigration.label: Border security plus legal immigration; those 'who broke the law and came here illegally should not be given a free path to citizenship' (Charlottesville Tomorrow)

taxes.label: Simplify tax filing; balance the budget primarily by attacking fraudulent federal spending (Cardinal News)

climate.label: Criticizes energy-production restrictions; supports American energy production; localities should decide on data centers (Charlottesville Tomorrow)
